Bulgaria votes for president in wake of deadly Black Sea drone strikes

Reuters

25 October, 2026 06:00 am IST

By Alex Lefkowitz SOFIA, Oct 25 (Reuters) – Bulgarians vote in presidential elections on Sunday as Russia’s war in Ukraine spreads to the waters off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast.

Polls place acting President Iliana Iotova, 61, and ex-caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, as leaders in a race of 27 candidates.

While the presidency is largely ceremonial, Sunday’s vote has taken on added significance after a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast that likely killed some two-dozen international seafarers.

Show Full Article

The strikes, which sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine, prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security.

Bulgaria has stopped short of directly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome “benefits the Russian Federation”.

Both leading presidential candidates condemned the strikes, but they differ over the broader war.

Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier.

“I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe. A reliable NATO ally that defends its interests through preparedness, strong diplomacy and a clear position,” he said at a rally on Thursday.

Iotova, formerly vice president, became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter the parliamentary race, which he won on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket. Radev supports Iotova and they both call for a diplomatic end to the war.

A victory for Iotova would make her Bulgaria’s first elected female president.

“My opponents argue that there must be a war of attrition.” she told a rally on Thursday. “The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted.”

Polls by Alpha Research give Iotova 41% of the vote and Gyurov 28%. If no candidate wins a majority, a runoff vote will be held on November 1.

Voting starts at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and polls close at 8 p.m.

(Editing by Edward McAllister and Ros Russell)

North Korea’s Kim Jong Un returns from China after war memorial visit, state media says

Reuters

25 October, 2026 04:00 am IST

Facebook

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

By Cynthia Kim and Joyce Lee SEOUL, Oct 25 (Reuters) – North Korean leader Kim Jong Un returned to his country by road on Sunday after visiting a historic Korean War memorial in the Chinese border city of Dandong, North Korean state media reported.

Kim visited the city on Saturday and crossed a newly opened bridge that connects the country to its biggest trading partner, China, which was seen as symbolizing a push by Beijing and Pyongyang to expand trade ties.

North Korean state media heavily emphasized the historical weight of the visit, describing the bilateral relationship as an “unbreakable” bond forged during the 1950-1953 conflict.

Show Full Article

Kim stated during his tour that the North Korean people would “forever remember the glorious years of fighting alongside the Chinese people” and pass down “generational gratitude to the Chinese people who helped our revolution with blood,” according to the KCNA.

The visit is seen as a renewed push by China and North Korea to bolster their economic relationship ahead of a trip to the region by US President Donald Trump next month. It also highlights a sophisticated diplomatic balancing act by Pyongyang, which has been deepening military ties with Moscow in the past two years.

Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025 for a military parade, and Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korea in June.

“Enjoying a bird’s-eye view at the middle point of the newly-inaugurated bridge, Comrade Kim Jong Un expressed expectation that the bridge would undoubtedly and correctly fulfill its historic mission of linking the two countries and firmly joining the minds of the peoples of the two countries,” KCNA reported.

The two Koreas are technically at war after their 1950-53 war ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

(Reporting by Cynthia Kim, Joyce Lee; Editing by David Gregorio and Alistair Bell)
